name: Residue — Unmoderated Shelf Broadcast Board
description: Residue is the Shelf's own answer to the sanitized corporate net — a chaotic, unmoderated broadcast board that runs on a patchwork of salvaged servers, ghost-net relays, and volunteer node-runners across the lowest tiers of Meridian 88. Unlike more sophisticated Underworld boards, Residue requires no BCI, no verified identity, and no hardware above a decade-old neural-tap or even a basic screen terminal, making it genuinely accessible to the most hardware-poor Shelf residents. The platform hosts everything from hyperlocal mutual aid coordination and ghost market schedules to raw trauma-dumps, art drops, and the kind of unfiltered political rage that gets scrubbed from every corporate-adjacent platform within minutes.
cultural_impact: Residue functions as the de facto public square, emergency broadcast system, and confessional booth for Tier 1 Meridian 88, and its chaotic authenticity has made it a source of raw cultural material that Tier 3-4 artists mine (often without credit or compensation) for 'Shelf aesthetic' projects. During the 2218 Shelf flooding crisis, Residue's mutual aid boards coordinated relief faster than any official channel, cementing its reputation as infrastructure rather than mere social media.
key_figures: Pax Nwachukwu-Orin (original node architect, whereabouts unknown)
The Bucket Collective (rotating volunteer moderation crew, loosely defined)
Yemisi Strand (Shelf journalist who broke three major Corponation scandals via Residue leaks)
locations: Distributed across Shelf node-runner apartments, Row 3-17
The Sump, a Tier 1 server collective under the old lakefront infrastructure
Public terminal clusters at Shelf Market Row and the Underpass Commons
story_hooks: A Corponation data-scrubbing team has identified Residue's core node architecture and is preparing to collapse it during a major ghost market weekend — someone on the inside is trying to warn the Bucket Collective without exposing themselves.

A series of anonymous posts on Residue describe, in precise technical detail, a vulnerability in the city's water reclamation system — and it's unclear whether this is a whistleblower, a threat, or someone testing whether anyone in power is actually watching.

A Tier 4 journalist wants to do an 'authentic Shelf voices' piece using Residue posts as source material — their fixer, a Shelf native, has to decide how much of their community to expose for a story that may or may not help anyone.
user_base: Estimated 2-4 million irregular users across Tier 1; exact figures impossible due to no registration requirement; heaviest usage among 16-35 Shelf residents
monetization: No monetization; sustained entirely by volunteer node-runners and occasional anonymous crypto-donations routed through Underworld relay accounts
notable_feature: Hardware-floor accessibility — the platform is engineered to function on any networked device manufactured after 2160, including devices with no BCI compatibility, ensuring access for the most economically marginalized users in M88
